claims.text: A dense alumina (Al2O3) ceramic coating reduces liquid-aluminum corrosion of dipping and plating equipment parts relative to uncoated metal parts.
Standard metal components such as steel are susceptible to corrosion by high-temperature liquid aluminum.
The proposed intervention is deposition of a dense, high-quality alumina ceramic coating on component surfaces.
The intended operating environment involves prolonged exposure to high-temperature liquid aluminum during hot-dip processing.
The deposited alumina coating forms a continuous, low-porosity layer.
The continuous, low-porosity alumina layer acts as a physical barrier between liquid aluminum and the metal substrate.
Alumina has excellent thermal stability under the proposed hot-dip conditions.
Alumina has low reactivity with liquid aluminum.
Alumina has a low diffusion rate relevant to transport between liquid aluminum and the underlying metal.
The alumina coating prevents or retards direct contact between liquid aluminum and the underlying metal substrate.
Retarding contact and diffusion between liquid aluminum and the substrate reduces corrosion.
Alumina-coated parts will have significantly lower corrosion rates than uncoated parts.
Alumina-coated parts will have longer service lives than uncoated parts.
Uncoated steel components undergo rapid corrosion under comparable high-temperature liquid-aluminum exposure.
The protective effect depends on the alumina coating remaining intact without cracking or spallation.
The coating's performance may be limited to the liquid-aluminum temperatures and contact durations typical of industrial hot-dip processes.
Long-term alumina-coating durability under cyclic thermal stress and mechanical abrasion is uncertain.
